LESSON: PUTTING

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.8: Putting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Putting. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. collect different groups of similar objects for counting
2. identify sets of similar objects in the environment for counting
3. put similar objects together with a sum not exceeding 9
4. enjoy the activities of putting together objects in their day to day experiences e) appreciate that things become more when put together e.g. 1 little brown bird sitting on a wall along came another one and that made two. 63 objects to get sums of not more than nine (9) using ICT devices. programmes on the concept of putting together.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. collect different groups of similar objects for counting
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to collect different groups of similar objects for counting. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify sets of similar objects in the environment for counting
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify sets of similar objects in the environment for counting. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. put similar objects together with a sum not exceeding 9
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to put similar objects together with a sum not exceeding 9. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. enjoy the activities of putting together objects in their day to day experiences e) appreciate that things become more when put together e.g. 1 little brown bird sitting on a wall along came another one and that made two. 63 objects to get sums of not more than nine (9) using ICT devices. programmes on the concept of putting together.

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Putting.
2. Explain Putting to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Putting.
4. Show that you can: collect different groups of similar objects for counting
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Putting. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Putting important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. collect different groups of similar objects for counting
2. identify sets of similar objects in the environment for counting
3. put similar objects together with a sum not exceeding 9
4. enjoy the activities of putting together objects in their day to day experiences e) appreciate that things become more when put together e.g. 1 little brown bird sitting on a wall along came another one and that made two. 63 objects to get sums of not more than nine (9) using ICT devices. programmes on the concept of putting together.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
